newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Feb 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Feb 14.

text.p: MLADA FRONTA DNES - The Republican Party has already obstructed discussions in parliament on the Czech-German declaration for a few days, which led Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus to call a cabinet meeting in parliament. After a nearly one hour debate, Klaus and certain ministers from the Civic Democratic Party conceded that the cabinet could suggest to the Supreme Court to ban the Republicans.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The Czech-Moravian school workers union was given a proposal from Education Minister Ivan Pilip, which could lead to an agreement to end the strike before it enters its third week. According to the chairman of the union, Jaroslav Rossler, the union will make its decision on February 21 whether to sign the agreement.
- The Czech National Bank had losses in 1996 of 8.7 billion crowns. This result will evaluated by an external auditor.

PRAVO - Foreign agricultural trade ended last year with a deficit of 22.3 billion crowns, nearly twice as much as in 1995. Agricultural trade made up 13.92 percent of all foreign trade, which is a year-on-year increase of 0.76 percent.

- Zemska Banka lost the authority to trade on the Prague Stock Exchange, according to a spokesman for the exchange, Milan Vodicka. The Finance Ministry discontinued its licence for stock trading due to a violation of one aspect of securities law.

LIDOVE NOVINY - During February, the Czech Army should receive an offer from the Russian company Rosvooruzhenie for a supply of military technology. This should be offered as a payment of the interest on Russia's debt to the Czech Republic, which amounts to nearly 3.5 billion dollars.

- Health Minister Jan Strasky appointed his deputy, Josef Suchopar, as temporary director of General Faculty Hospital in Prague to replace Dana Kocourkova, who resigned yesterday. A new director for the hospital, which owes several hundred million crowns to Vseobecna Zdravotni Pojistovna, must be chosen by March 15, according to a court ruling.
